notes: A new strategy and testing framework would likely draw on NRW's role on special sites and water receptors (SI4); the funding question and renewed attention to PCB tips around Wrexham signal rising public and political pressure.
summary: On 30 September 2026 a Senedd member debate led by Niamh Salkeld MS won cross-party support for a polluter pays approach to historic contaminated land, a national framework to test and assess potentially contaminated sites, more support for councils, and a UK Government funding mechanism where costs cannot be recovered. Farmers Weekly reported on 5 October 2026 that the Welsh Government called contaminated land a key priority and pledged a Wales-wide strategy to restore post-industrial land, strengthening the polluter pays principle. NRW said a 2015 survey had identified more than 9,000 potential sites needing investigation and that farmland near historic sites was monitored by risk rather than routinely.
title: Senedd backs a polluter pays approach and a national testing framework for contaminated land; Welsh Government pledges a Wales-wide strategy
